summary: TUI render cost: per-message rendered-row cache (a streaming delta re-renders only its message; rows are Arc-shared so reassembly copies pointers); the project checkpoint no longer carries the transcript and transcript/stream mutations no longer dirty it; checkpoint/layout writes wait for 1 s of input quiet; the unconditional 250 ms checkpoint-tick redraw and 20 ms pairing redraw are gone (pairing redraws on key or once per second for its countdown); the 500 ms session-browser refresh redraws only when its projection changed; lapsed footer/copy notices clear themselves. The event-loop wait still honours the ordinary paste-burst deadline (ordinary_paste_wait, already present).

notes: Deviations: (1) tests outside the owned path: new tests/tui_idle_cost.rs drives the production loop via TuiHarness (needs its own process for ZENPI_HOME); four existing tests encoded transcript-in-checkpoint and were updated (budget crowding now uses arch console messages). (2) The session-browser 500 ms refresh redrew unconditionally at 2 Hz; not named in the row but required by the quiet-idle validator. (3) Expiring footer/copy notices previously relied on the 250 ms tick; they now clear on expiry. Already existed: the event-loop timeout already included the paste-burst deadline (ordinary_paste_wait); only a validator was added. Kept: the arch console log stays in the checkpoint draft (no other durable owner, not dirtied by streaming); legacy 'messages' fields in old checkpoints are ignored and the session journal reloads the transcript. The loop still polls at the 100 ms poll interval to service runtime/mailbox sources (no draw, no write). Streaming-frame reassembly is O(min(rows, MAX_RENDER_LINES)) pointer copies, hence the residual 2.6 -> 4.9 ms in a debug build.
